label: Brisnik: MISC3
title: Agomelatine in a person aged 75 or over
statement: Prescribed agomelatine - and the patient is aged ≥ 75 years

source.document: Brisnik V, et al. Deprescribing of antidepressants: indicators of high-risk and overprescribing. BMC Med 2024;22:193, Tables 3-4
source.citation: Brisnik V, Vukas J, Jung-Sievers C, et al. Deprescribing of antidepressants: development of indicators of high-risk and overprescribing using the RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method. BMC Med 2024;22:193. doi:10.1186/s12916-024-03397-w

An earlier version expressed it as a formal rule. ClinicaLANTERN added the summary, medicine list, screening instructions and fictional histories. The authors have not endorsed these additions.

plain_summary: Agomelatine is not recommended in people aged 75 or over, because there is little evidence it works at that age and it can harm the liver.
rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when agomelatine (Group A) is supplied to a person whose age on the history is 75 or over. If age at supply is missing, report only a possible finding and ask the pharmacist to confirm it. A person aged 74 or under is not a finding.
cannot_be_seen: Why agomelatine was started, liver test results that are missing from this record, and whether the age recorded is right on the day of each supply. Supplies from a hospital or another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: Whether agomelatine is still suitable at this age, including a check of liver function, and whether a review is suitable.
